# fft_analysis.m
# Single-sided amplitude spectrum and peak detection with the FFT.
# Written from scratch for the matlab-to-python-agent demo (public, no client data).

import numpy as np # MATLAB: implicit
import scipy.signal # MATLAB: implicit
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt # MATLAB: implicit

fs = 500;                          # sampling rate (Hz)
N  = 1000;                         # number of samples
t  = np.arange(0, N)/fs; # MATLAB: (0:N-1)/fs -> np.arange(0, N)/fs

x = 1.0*np.sin(2*np.pi*50*t) + 0.5*np.sin(2*np.pi*120*t) + 0.25*np.cos(2*np.pi*200*t); # MATLAB: sin -> np.sin, cos -> np.cos

X  = np.fft.fft(x); # MATLAB: fft -> np.fft.fft
P2 = np.abs(X/N);                     # two-sided spectrum # MATLAB: abs -> np.abs
P1 = P1_sub = P2[0:int(N/2)+1];                  # keep DC .. Nyquist # MATLAB: 1:N/2+1 -> 0:int(N/2)+1
P1 = P1.copy()
P1[1:-1] = 2*P1[1:-1];       # fold negative frequencies in # MATLAB: 2:end-1 -> 1:-1
f  = fs*(np.arange(0, int(N/2)+1))/N;               # frequency axis (Hz) # MATLAB: 0:(N/2) -> np.arange(0, int(N/2)+1)

idx = np.argmax(P1); # MATLAB: [~, idx]  = max(P1) -> np.argmax
peak_freq = f[idx];                # strongest component

locs, _ = scipy.signal.find_peaks(P1, height=0.1); # MATLAB: findpeaks -> scipy.signal.find_peaks
pk = P1[locs]
peak_freqs = f[locs];

total_power    = np.sum(x**2)/N;      # time-domain power # MATLAB: sum -> np.sum
spectral_power = np.sum(np.abs(X)**2)/N**2;   # Parseval check # MATLAB: sum -> np.sum, abs -> np.abs
